subproblem.title: Derivative bounds and measurability for a map that is 1-Lipschitz on a closed ball (Simon 4.5 (14)-(16), step 1)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ), LipschitzOnWith 1 f (closedBall 0 r) → Measurable (fun x => hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ j : Fin ℓ, Measurable (gradient (fun y => f y j))) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) r, hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ f x) ≤ n ∧ ∀ j : Fin ℓ, ‖gradient (fun y => f y j) x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ ball 0 r → ∀ j : Fin ℓ, ‖gradient (fun y => f y j) x‖ ^ 2 ≤ hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ f x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is step 1 of the parent proof (Simon 4.5 (14)-(16)), stated for an arbitrary radius r.

Notation.
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i in Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of R^n, so ||e_i|| = 1.
- For a continuous linear map A : R^n -> R^l, ||A|| is the operator norm and hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2.
- pi_j := EuclideanSpace.proj j : R^l -> R is the continuous linear j-th coordinate map, so f^j = pi_j o f. For every w in R^l, |w_j| <= ||w|| (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
- T := InnerProductSpace.toDual R (R^n) is the Riesz linear isometric equivalence, T v = <v, .>. By definition, gradient h x = T^{-1}(fderiv R h x) for h : R^n -> R.

1. Measurability.
 - By measurable_fderiv, x -> fderiv R f x is measurable into the Borel space R^n ->L[R] R^l.
 - The map A -> hsNormSq A is continuous. For each i, A -> A e_i is the continuous linear evaluation map (ContinuousLinearMap.apply); norm and squaring are continuous; and a finite sum of continuous maps is continuous.
 - Continuous maps are measurable, so x -> |Df(x)|^2 is measurable.
 - For each j, x -> fderiv R f^j x is measurable by measurable_fderiv, and T^{-1} is continuous. Hence grad f^j = T^{-1} o (fderiv R f^j) is measurable.
 This proves (a).
2. (b) holds because hsNormSq(fderiv R f x) is a finite sum of squares of real numbers.
3. Neighbourhoods. If x is in ball 0 r, then closedBall 0 r is a neighbourhood of x: ball 0 r is open, contains x, and is contained in closedBall 0 r.
4. Bound for |Df|^2. Let x be in ball 0 r.
 - f is 1-Lipschitz on closedBall 0 r, a neighbourhood of x (step 3), so norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn gives ||fderiv R f x|| <= 1.
 - For any A and i, ||A e_i|| <= ||A|| ||e_i|| = ||A||, so hsNormSq A <= sum_{i<n} ||A||^2 = n ||A||^2.
 - Hence |Df(x)|^2 <= n ||fderiv R f x||^2 <= n.
5. Bound for grad f^j. Fix j.
 - For y, z in closedBall 0 r: |f^j(y) - f^j(z)| = |(f(y) - f(z))_j| <= ||f(y) - f(z)|| <= ||y - z||. So f^j is 1-Lipschitz on closedBall 0 r.
 - For x in ball 0 r, norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn (with step 3) gives ||fderiv R f^j x|| <= 1.
 - T^{-1} is an isometry, so ||grad f^j(x)|| = ||fderiv R f^j x|| <= 1.
 Steps 4 and 5 prove (c).
6. Rademacher. LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem is Rademacher's theorem for a map between finite-dimensional real normed spaces that is Lipschitz on a set, with respect to the additive Haar measure volume. It gives, for a.e. x: if x is in closedBall 0 r, then f is differentiable within closedBall 0 r at x. Let x be such a point that lies in ball 0 r. Since closedBall 0 r is a neighbourhood of x (step 3), f is differentiable at x (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt).
7. Chain rule. For such an x and any j, f^j = pi_j o f with pi_j continuous linear. So f^j has derivative pi_j o (fderiv R f x) at x, that is, fderiv R f^j x = pi_j o (fderiv R f x) (HasFDerivAt.comp, HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
8. Coordinates of the gradient. Put g := grad f^j(x). Then T g = fderiv R f^j x (toDual_gradient). So, for each i in Fin n, by step 7:
 g_i = <g, e_i> = (T g)(e_i) = (fderiv R f^j x)(e_i) = ((fderiv R f x)(e_i))_j.
9. Comparison. By EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq and step 8,
 ||g||^2 = sum_i g_i^2 = sum_i (((fderiv R f x)(e_i))_j)^2 <= sum_i ||(fderiv R f x)(e_i)||^2 = |Df(x)|^2,
 using |w_j| <= ||w|| termwise. The null set excluded in step 6 does not depend on j. So for a.e. x, if x is in ball 0 r, the inequality holds for every j. This proves (d). QED
proof_key_steps: measurable_fderiv, together with continuity of A -> hsNormSq A and of the inverse Riesz map T^{-1}, gives the measurability claims; |Df|^2 >= 0 as a sum of squares.
closedBall 0 r is a neighbourhood of every x in ball 0 r, so norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn gives ||Df(x)|| <= 1 and hence |Df(x)|^2 <= n ||Df(x)||^2 <= n.
Each coordinate f^j is 1-Lipschitz on closedBall 0 r (|w_j| <= ||w||), so ||grad f^j(x)|| = ||D f^j(x)|| <= 1 on ball 0 r (the Riesz map is an isometry).
Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem): f is differentiable at a.e. x in ball 0 r.
At such x, D f^j(x) = proj_j o Df(x), so (grad f^j(x))_i = (Df(x) e_i)_j and ||grad f^j(x)||^2 = sum_i (Df(x) e_i)_j^2 <= |Df(x)|^2.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type agree, including arbitrary dimensions and radius. Each conjunct follows from the supplied steps: measurable_fderiv and the Riesz isometry give measurability; interior Lipschitz bounds control both derivatives; Rademacher and the coordinate chain rule give the squared-gradient comparison on a common full-measure set. The comparison is correctly restricted to almost every point. The proof is complete and non-circular.
